slides.title: What you will be able to do
objectives: Differentiate a procurement plan from a project plan
Select a packaging strategy for given constraints

slides.title: Why this matters
body: Procurement shapes cost, risk, and timing across the whole project.
- Sets the commercial framework for every vendor relationship
- Locks in risk allocation before any vendor is chosen
- Determines delivery leverage for the life of the project

slides.title: What is a procurement plan

media.placeholder: photo of signed contract on desk

bullets: A document that defines how purchases will be managed
Covers vendor selection, contract type, and delivery timing

slides.title: Objectives and criteria
body: - Clear measurable targets aligned to sponsor expectations
slides.key_message: Tie every criterion to a sponsor-owned success measure.

slides.title: Scope and packaging
body: - Balance integration risk against vendor leverage

slides.title: Contract type
body: - Fixed-price: risk sits with the vendor, less flexibility
- Time-and-materials: flexibility, risk on the buyer
slides.key_message: Contract type is the single biggest risk-allocation lever in the plan.

slides.title: Knowledge check
slides.stem: Which of these belongs in a procurement plan, not a project plan?
slides.feedback_correct: Contract type is a core procurement-plan decision — it shapes risk allocation and payment structure.
slides.feedback_incorrect: That option is a general project-management concern. Contract type (option 3) is the procurement answer.

slides.title: Key takeaways
takeaways: A procurement plan answers 'how will we buy?' — distinct from the project plan
Packaging and contract type allocate risk before any vendor is involved
Every criterion should trace back to a sponsor-owned success measure
